page.layout: One printed page (right page) of running text in one column, with the running head and page number at the top and a catchword at the lower right. The left edge of the neighbouring page is visible at the left and is not transcribed. No margin notes and no footnotes.

main_text.p: Nec mouamur audaculas istas locustas, quan-quam fastigio[?] turgentes, capillis mulierum, ac dentibus leonum armatas, quae est eorum nota iam, & perspecta omnibus lasciuia cum sanguinaria crudelitate coniuncta. Utcun-que præ se ferant equorum speciem, qui iam ad bellum parantur: quae omnia furores istos præmonstrant, quos illi in sanctos quotidie excitant, coniurationes, bella, cædes, clades, quas per orbem terrarum, per singulas regiones, per oppida, per domos, armis, venefi-ciis, puluere tormentario, secretis conspirationibus meditantur, & concitant: utcunque libera[?] palam in furores ferantur, ut furentem ipsorum audaciam nec cohibere, nec dissimulare possint: Nos tamen in Christi aduen-tum spe atque expectatione propendentes, omnia pericula, quæ nobis propter veritatem intentantur, vel contemnendo, vel subeundo, magno animo, hoc est, Christiana tolerantia vincimus.

page.notes: The centre of the text block is heavily damaged by a dark stain and show-through, so several words are doubtful. "fastigio" is read from the broken letters at the start of the second line of the paragraph. "libera" (after "utcunque") is doubtful; the word may be different. "Utcun-que" is printed with a capital V, read as the vowel U. The lines "eundo, magno animo, hoc est, / Christiana tolerantia / vincimus." are centred in the printed block and are kept within the paragraph. The catchword "SECVN-" is printed at the lower right.
